Day 33 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

host_vars, group_vars & register

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Real projects need static per-host/group data and runtime results without mixing both into one giant variable file.

Architecture / mental model

group_vars + host_vars + task output(register) → effective runtime data → later tasks

How it works

`group_vars` stores data shared by inventory groups and `host_vars` stores data specific to individual hosts. The directory structure keeps inventory-related data close to the model it describes.

`register` captures the structured result of a task for later decisions. Return data can include stdout, stderr, return codes, changed state and module-specific fields.

Static inventory data and runtime observations solve different problems. Keeping them separate makes it easier to see which value is configuration and which value was discovered during this execution.

Hands-on reference

ansible-inventory -i inventory.ini --host web01
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml -vv

Verification

Use a debug task in a lab to inspect a registered result, then remove broad debug output before production if it could expose sensitive data.

Field note / gotcha

Registered variables exist for the current playbook run; they are not a durable state store. If you need persistent truth, put it somewhere designed to persist.

Security considerations

Registered output can contain tokens, command output or other secrets. Use `no_log` appropriately and avoid dumping whole result objects into CI logs.

What I learned

Automation gets clearer when configuration data and observed runtime data have different homes.
